svg.text: Spend writer: gateway requests land in the proxy's own tables
Request record (observer queue)
key, user, team, end user, deployment,
usage, cost, timings, user agent,
spend_logs_metadata (team, key, hooks)
off the request path; never blocks it
Added up in memory
spend per key, user, team, member,
end user; daily rows per entity, day,
key, model, provider, endpoint;
spend log rows queued (cap 10k)
Timers (as the proxy)
spend logs: every 2 s
everything else: proxy_batch_write_at
(default 10 s) plus 0-5 s jitter
shutdown: drain the queue, then flush
Proxy Postgres, same statements and order as the Python writer
LiteLLM_SpendLogs: batches of 100, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; columns and 49-key metadata as the proxy writes them
user, end user, key (spend, total_spend, last_active), team, team membership: spend += cost, ids sorted, lock_timeout 5 s
update-only for users, keys and teams; end users created unblocked; membership only for users on the team roster
LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend / DailyTeamSpend / DailyEndUserSpend: upsert that adds tokens, requests, spend; model_group kept from first insert
every write adds to what is stored, so gateway replicas and Python proxies can write side by side
deadlock, lock timeout, lost connection: 3 retries with backoff; then daily rows and spend logs are kept for the next flush,
entity spend is dropped (as the proxy drops it)
Read by what already reads these tables
proxy UI usage pages, /spend and /global/activity endpoints, key and team spend shown in the admin UI,
and the proxy's own budget checks on its next key lookup
